title: Black Garlic and Date Hoisin-Style Sauce
description: White beans, black garlic and dates blend into a thick hoisin-style dipping sauce with a warm hint of star anise.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: mild white miso
ingredients.note: Use plain white miso, ideally no more than 215 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/2 tsp total.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: For a plain infusion, steep sliced mushrooms in hot water, strain and add no salt. Estimate assumes 15 mg sodium per cup.

steps.title: Plump the dates
steps.text: Simmer {da} in {mu} with {ani} for 4 minutes until the date pieces soften.

steps.title: Blend the bean base
steps.text: Add {be2}, {gar}, {mis}, {a}, {rv} and {tah}. Take the pan off the heat and blend until glossy and completely smooth.

steps.title: Set the texture
steps.text: Return to low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring. The sauce should hold a soft line when a spoon is drawn through it.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Serve as a dip for tender pork or duck, or loosen a spoonful in warm cooking juices for a finishing glaze.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use 1/2 tsp mild white miso in place of 1 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, halve the black garlic and use only 1 teaspoon rice vinegar. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 75 kcal, 2.7 g protein, 11.9 g total carbohydrate, 2.2 g fat, 1.9 g fiber, 151 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 70 kcal, 2.7 g protein, 10.7 g total carbohydrate, 2.1 g fat, 1.8 g fiber, 57 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
